summary: Howe and Klevdal reinterpret basic local Shimura varieties and their non-minuscule analogues as moduli of neutral admissible pairs (families of B_dR^+-latticed isocrystals whose modified bundles are semistable of slope 0), for any connected linear algebraic group G. On the way they extend to non-reductive G the basic strata of Bun_G (Theorem 4.2.2), the B_dR^+-affine Grassmannian and its Schubert cells (Theorem 5.0.4, Proposition 5.2.1), the admissible loci (Propositions 7.3.3–7.3.4) and basic duality (Theorem 8.5.1). They relate lattices and filtrations over diamonds (Theorems 3.2.1, 3.3.1), build period domains of p-adic Hodge structures, and show that Hodge and Hodge–Tate loci of tensors and the resulting special subdiamonds are closed, including for non-reductive subgroups (Propositions 6.4.1, 7.5.2). The main theorem is a bi-analytic Ax–Lindemann theorem (Theorem 9.1.3, Theorem A in the minuscule case). For the two analytic structures on a basic infinite-level space given by the Hodge and Hodge–Tate towers, the Zariski closure in one structure of an irreducible analytic set of the other is a special subvariety, so the closed bi-analytic sets are exactly the special subvarieties. Theorem B is the sideways version for any neutral admissible pair over a rigid variety. The proof uses the Tannakian formalism, a Baire-category argument for Hodge-generic classical points (Lemma 9.3.1), Part I's openness of Galois images and a constant-rank computation. The atlas plans the reductive foundations (Bun_G, Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannians, local shtuka moduli, relative Fargues–Fontaine curves, period sheaves). It has none of the theory of admissible pairs, Part I included, so this is routed to one new roadmap. Five general inputs go to their owners as sources: seminormal full faithfulness to D6, Scholze's functor M to P8, B(G, μ) to BG1, the Rapoport–Viehmann and Gleason–Lourenço inputs to HS2, and Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev to LD.6. Two small Part IIs take general facts on algebraic groups and on rigid-analytic Zariski geometry. Fourteen source issues are recorded: twelve misprints, one gap (the proof of Theorem 7.2.3 for singular bases), and v1's incorrect Lemma 4.1.1, already corrected in v2.

items.name: Admissible pairs and basic admissible pairs over C (Part I)
items.statement: Let C/Q_p be an algebraically closed non-archimedean extension and B_dR^+ = B_dR^+(C). (1) A B_dR^+-latticed isocrystal is a pair (W, L) with W an isocrystal over Q̆_p and L ⊆ W ⊗_{Q̆_p} B_dR a B_dR^+-lattice; a morphism (W, L) → (W', L') is a morphism of isocrystals f with f(L) ⊆ L', strict if f(L) = f(W)_{B_dR} ∩ L'. (2) An admissible pair is a B_dR^+-latticed isocrystal (W, L_ét) such that the modification E(W)_{L_ét} at ∞ of the vector bundle E(W) on the Fargues–Fontaine curve FF_{C♭} is semistable of slope zero. (3) It is basic if the slope decomposition W = ⊕_λ W_λ induces L = ⊕_λ L_λ with L_λ = (W_λ ⊗ B_dR) ∩ L. AdmPair(C) ⊇ AdmPair^basic(C) are the resulting categories.
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Definition 5.1.1; recalled in Section 1.3, p. 9 and used in Definition 7.1.1, p. 39

items.name: p-adic Hodge structures over C (Part I)
items.statement: A B_dR^+-latticed Q_p-vector space (V, L) (V finite-dimensional over Q_p, L ⊆ V ⊗_{Q_p} B_dR a B_dR^+-lattice) is a p-adic Hodge structure of weight λ ∈ Q if the modification (V ⊗_{Q_p} O_FF)_L at ∞_C is semistable of slope −λ/2. The category HS(C) of p-adic Hodge structures is the full subcategory of Q-graded B_dR^+-latticed Q_p-vector spaces whose degree-λ part has weight λ.
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Definition 4.2.1; used in Definition 6.0.1, p. 35

items.name: HS(C) and AdmPair(C) are connected neutral Tannakian; basic admissible pairs are p-adic Hodge structures (Part I)
items.statement: (1) HS(C) is abelian and is a connected neutral Tannakian category over Q_p with fibre functor ω_ét: (V, L) ↦ V. (2) AdmPair(C) is a connected neutral Tannakian category with fibre functor ω_ét = H^0(FF_{C♭}, E(W)_{L_ét}); it is equivalent to the isogeny category of rigidified Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules; and (ω_ét, ω_{L_dR}), with ω_{L_dR} the de Rham lattice c_dR^{-1}(W ⊗ B_dR^+), is an equivalence of Tannakian categories ω_HS: AdmPair^basic(C) ≅ HS(C), the weight grading coming from the slope decomposition.
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Lemma 4.3.2, Theorem 4.3.5 and Theorem 5.1.6; used in Section 6, p. 36, Lemma 6.2.1, p. 36, Proposition 6.2.3, p. 37, Theorem 7.1.2, p. 40, and Section 8.3, p. 51

items.name: Motivic Galois groups and the canonical reduction of structure group (Part I)
items.statement: Let T be a neutral Tannakian category over Q_p with fibre functor ω, G/Q_p a linear algebraic group and 𝒢: Rep G → T an exact tensor functor with ω∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std. The Tannakian subcategory ⟨𝒢⟩ generated by the image has tensor-automorphism group Aut^⊗(ω|_⟨𝒢⟩), a linear algebraic group which a trivialization ω∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std embeds as a closed subgroup H ≤ G; 𝒢 has a canonical reduction of structure group to H (a factorization Rep G → Rep H → T), and H is the stabilizer in G of the lines ℓ ⊆ ω(𝒢(V)), V ∈ Rep G, that underlie rank-one subobjects of 𝒢(V) (for p-adic Hodge structures: the Hodge–Tate lines).
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Sections 2.1, 2.1.3 and 4.5; used in Section 6.1, p. 36, Section 7.2, p. 41, and Lemma 7.5.1, p. 46

items.name: Filtrations, lattices and bilatticed G-bundles over a point; goodness and type (Part I)
items.statement: Let G be a connected linear algebraic group over a field K ⊆ C and B^+ = B_dR^+(C) with fraction field B (or C[[t]] ⊆ C((t))). A filtration (resp. lattice) on a G-bundle ω: Rep G → Vect is an exact tensor functor to filtered vector spaces (resp. B^+-latticed spaces) with an identification of its underlying functor with ω. A bilatticed G-bundle ω_bl (two lattices on one G(B)-bundle) is good of type [μ] if its relative position in G(B^+)\G(B)/G(B^+) is the double coset of μ(t), t a uniformizer of B^+; for non-reductive G these double cosets do not exhaust G(B). The Bialynicki-Birula functors BB_1, BB_2 take the trace filtration of one lattice on the reduction of the other.
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Definition 3.1.5 and Sections 3.1–3.2; used in Section 3, p. 19

items.name: Goodness of a bilatticed G-bundle is exactness of either trace filtration (Part I)
items.statement: For a bilatticed G-bundle ω_bl the following are equivalent: (1) ω_bl is good; (2) BB_1∘ω_bl is a filtered G-bundle (i.e. is exact); (3) BB_2∘ω_bl is a filtered G-bundle. In this case, if ω_bl has type [μ], then BB_1∘ω_bl has type [μ^{-1}] and BB_2∘ω_bl has type [μ].
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Theorem 3.2.6; used in the proof of Theorem 3.2.1, p. 22

items.name: Types can only go up under representations when a lattice is not good (Part I)
items.statement: Let G be a connected linear algebraic group over C with Levi decomposition G = M ⋉ U, g = mu ∈ G(C((t))), and [μ] the conjugacy class of cocharacters of M with m ∈ M(C[[t]]) t^μ M(C[[t]]). For any representation ρ: G → GL_n, if [ν] indexes the Schubert cell containing ρ(g), then [ν] ≥ [ρ∘μ] in the Bruhat order. If ρ is faithful, then [ν] = [ρ∘μ] if and only if g ∈ G(C[[t]]) t^μ G(C[[t]]).
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Theorem 3.5.1; used in the proof of Proposition 5.2.1, p. 34, after identifying B_dR^+(C) ≅ C[[t]] (Part I Example 3.0.1)

items.name: When the filtration determines the lattice (Part I)
items.statement: (1) If the weights of [μ] in the adjoint action on Lie G are ≤ 1, then BB: Gr_[μ](C) → Fl_[μ^{-1}](C) is a bijection (for G reductive this means [μ] is minuscule). (2) If a group 𝔊 acts on B^+ preserving its maximal ideal, K = C^𝔊 ⊆ L, 𝔊 acts on K·t through an infinite-order character, and G and [μ] are defined over K, then Fl_[μ^{-1}](K) is the set of 𝔊-invariants of Gr_[μ](C); this applies to K a p-adic field, C = K̄^, 𝔊 = Gal(K̄/K) (Part I Example 3.1.10).
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Proposition 3.1.7 and Example 3.1.10; used in Section 5.3, p. 34, and the proof of Theorem 5.0.4(5), p. 35

items.name: The Kottwitz set B(G, [μ^{-1}]) and basic classes for non-reductive G
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be a connected linear algebraic group with unipotent radical U and [μ] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p}. The projection G → G/U identifies B(G) = B(G/U) and the conjugacy classes of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p} and (G/U)_{Q̄_p}; B(G, [μ^{-1}]) is defined as B(G/U, [μ^{-1}]) through these identifications. A class is basic if its slope morphism is central in G. For G reductive B(G, [μ^{-1}]) has a unique basic class; in general, if M ⊆ G is a Levi subgroup, B(M, [μ^{-1}]) = B(G, [μ^{-1}]), but the basic class of M may fail to be central in G, and then B(G, [μ^{-1}]) has no basic class.
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 3; footnote 1; Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Section 4.4

items.name: The isocrystal of a good G-p-adic Hodge structure is the basic class (Part I)
items.statement: For a good G-p-adic Hodge structure 𝒢 over C whose weight morphism is central (for example if G = MT(𝒢)), the isocrystal class [b]_𝒢 of the associated G-admissible pair is the unique basic element of B(G, [μ^{-1}]_𝒢).
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Theorem 4.4.4; used in the proof of Proposition 6.2.3, p. 37

items.name: Existence of G-admissible pairs with given invariants (Part I)
items.statement: A Q̄_p-analytic (more generally C̄_0-analytic) G-admissible pair is good with invariants [μ] and b ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]); conversely, for every b ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]) there is a C̄_0-analytic G-admissible pair with invariants b and [μ]. (Choosing a Levi decomposition G = MU reduces to M reductive by push-out, where this is Rapoport–Viehmann, Proposition 3.1.)
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Example 5.4.6; used in Lemma 6.2.1, p. 36, and Proposition 7.3.3, p. 43

items.name: Admissible pairs with good reduction give crystalline Galois representations (Part I)
items.statement: Let K be a strict p-adic field and C = K̄^. The étale realization promotes to ω_{G_K}: AdmPair^goodred(K) → Rep_{Q_p}(G_K), which is fully faithful, has essential image stable under subobjects and consisting of crystalline representations.
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Theorem 5.5.1; used in the proof of Theorem 7.2.3, p. 42

items.name: The Galois image of an admissible pair with good reduction is open in its motivic Galois group (Part I)
items.statement: If 𝒢 is a G-admissible pair with good reduction over a strict p-adic field K and ρ: G_K → G(Q_p) is its Galois representation (after trivializing ω_ét∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std), then ρ(G_K) is an open subgroup of MG(𝒢)(Q_p). (ρ is Hodge–Tate, and by Serre's theorem on Hodge–Tate representations its image is open in its Zariski closure, which is MG(𝒢).)
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Corollary 5.5.3; used in the proof of Theorem 9.1.3, p. 57

items.name: Transcendence characterization of special points (Part I, Corollary C)
items.statement: Suppose b is basic and x ∈ M_{b,[μ]}(C). If π_{L_dR}(x) ∈ Gr_[μ^{-1}](C̄_0) and π_{L_ét}(x) ∈ Gr_[μ](C̄_0), then x is special. Conversely, if x is special, then π_{L_dR}(x) ∈ Gr_[μ^{-1}](Q̄_p) and π_{L_ét}(x) ∈ Gr_[μ](Q̄̆_p). (C_0 is the algebraic closure in C of the base field of Part I.)
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Corollary C (from Theorem B); cited in Remark 1.1.6, p. 6

items.name: Tannakian reconstruction of a linear algebraic group from its representations
items.statement: For a commutative Hopf algebra H over a field k (the coordinate ring of an affine group G), the A-points G(A) are identified, naturally in the commutative k-algebra A, with the tensor automorphisms of scalar extension to A on finite-dimensional H-comodules; in particular G = Aut^⊗(ω_std) on Rep G.
items.locator: Section 7.2, p. 41; 'there is a canonical identification of G with Aut^⊗(ω_std)', p. 41; also Section 6.1, p. 36
items.note: TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GroupFunctor.lean:138 and Tannaka/Equivalence.lean:188.

items.name: Neutral Tannakian categories are representation categories
items.statement: If T is a neutral Tannakian category over Q_p with fibre functor ω and T is generated by one object, Aut^⊗(ω) is a linear algebraic group over Q_p and ω induces T ≅ Rep Aut^⊗(ω) (Deligne–Milne, Theorem 2.11).
items.locator: Section 1.6, p. 12; reference to Deligne–Milne; used in Sections 6.1 and 7.2, pp. 36 and 41
items.note: MC.6 constructs tensor-automorphism groups of fibre functors of neutral Tannakian categories and proves the pro-algebraic reconstruction.

items.name: Levi decomposition of connected linear algebraic groups in characteristic zero
items.statement: A connected linear algebraic group G over a field of characteristic zero has a Levi decomposition G = M ⋉ U, U the unipotent radical and M ≅ G/U reductive, with any two Levi subgroups conjugate by U(k̄); the projection identifies conjugacy classes of cocharacters of G_{k̄} with those of M_{k̄}, and B(G) with B(M).
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 3; used in Remark 4.1.1, p. 26, Theorem 4.2.2, p. 27, Theorem 5.0.4, p. 31, and Proposition 7.3.4, p. 43
items.note: Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups plans the unipotent radical (Layer 5) and the Levi decomposition of parabolic subgroups (Layer 7), not Mostow's theorem for an arbitrary connected group.

items.name: The centre of a connected linear algebraic group is the kernel of the adjoint representation
items.statement: For G connected over a field of characteristic zero, Z(G) = ker(Ad: G → GL(Lie G)); hence b ∈ G(Q̆_p) is basic if and only if the isocrystal attached to b by the adjoint representation on Lie G is trivial.

items.name: Chevalley's theorem: closed subgroups are stabilizers of lines, in a countable family of representations
items.statement: Let G be a linear algebraic group over Q_p. (1) Every closed subgroup H ≤ G is the stabilizer of a line ℓ in some finite-dimensional representation of G. (2) Writing the regular representation Q_p[G] = ∪_i V_i as a countable filtered union of finite-dimensional subrepresentations, every closed subgroup is the stabilizer of a line in some exterior power ∧^j V_i (namely ∧^d(V_i ∩ I) for V_i containing generators of the ideal I of H).
items.locator: Proposition 9.3.4, p. 59; proof of (1), citing Borel, proof of Theorem 5.1; (1) is used in Propositions 6.4.1, p. 39, and 7.5.2, p. 47

items.name: Observable embeddings and quasi-affine homogeneous spaces
items.statement: (1) If G ≤ G' is an observable subgroup (the stabilizer of a vector in a representation of G'), then G'/G is quasi-affine (Thang–Bac, Theorem 9). (2) Every connected linear algebraic group G embeds as an observable subgroup of a reductive group: if ρ: G → GL_n is faithful, G is the stabilizer of a line in a representation of GL_n on which it acts through a character χ, and ρ × χ^{-1} embeds G into GL_n × G_m as an observable subgroup.

items.name: Homogeneous spaces of reductive groups by reductive subgroups are affine
items.statement: If G ≤ G' are both reductive, G'/G is affine (Matsushima), so a faithful representation realizes Gr_G as a Zariski closed subdiamond of Gr_{GL_n} in the reductive case.
items.note: Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 3 names the affine representability of G/H for reductive H (Matsushima).

items.name: Topology on rational points of algebraic varieties over p-adic fields
items.statement: For X of finite type over a p-adic field E, X(E) carries a functorial locally compact Hausdorff topology from affine charts; G(E) is a locally compact topological group; P(V)(Q_p) is compact with a countable basis of compact open subsets.
items.locator: Proposition 9.3.4, p. 59; proof of (2), p. 60; also compact open subgroups K ≤ G(Q_p) throughout Sections 8–9

items.name: Diamonds, small v-sheaves, underlying spaces and locally spatial diamonds
items.statement: The v-topology on perfectoid spaces is subcanonical; a small v-sheaf is a diamond if it is a quotient X/R by a pro-étale equivalence relation; any small v-sheaf Y has an underlying topological space |Y| of equivalence classes of geometric points; open subdiamonds correspond to open subsets of |Y|; spatial and locally spatial diamonds have spectral and locally spectral |Y|; maps of locally spatial diamonds are spectral and generalizing on |·|; locally spatial diamonds are closed under fibre products (Scholze, Étale cohomology of diamonds, §§8, 11, 12 and 14).

items.name: Locally closed subdiamonds from locally closed generalizing subsets
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond and D ⊆ |Y| a locally closed generalizing subset. Then Z := D ×_{|Y|} Y (the subsheaf of maps f with |f| factoring through D) is a locally spatial diamond with |Z| = D (subspace topology), and f: Y' → Y factors through Z if and only if |f| factors through D.
items.locator: Section 2.1, p. 13; p. 14 (the claim proved from ECD Proposition 11.20 and Lemma 7.3)
items.note: D5 plans ECD 11.17–11.31 (including 11.20, quasi-compact injections into locally spatial diamonds) and D1 plans ECD 7.1–7.7; the paper deduces the statement from these.

items.name: Diamondification of analytic adic spaces
items.statement: For Y an analytic adic space over Z_p, Y ↦ Y^♢ is a functor to diamonds with |Y| = |Y^♢|, Y_ét = Y^♢_ét and Y_fét = Y^♢_fét (ECD Lemma 15.6); diamonds over Spd L are small v-sheaves on Perfd_L.

items.name: Seminormal rigid analytic varieties embed fully faithfully in diamonds
items.statement: Let L be a non-archimedean field over Q_p. Y ↦ Y^♢ factors through seminormalization and is fully faithful on seminormal rigid analytic varieties over L (Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley Lectures, Proposition 10.2.3); for such Y, O_{Y_ét} is identified with the restriction of the v-structure sheaf O to Y^♢_ét.
items.note: D6 plans ECD Lemma 15.6 and says it is not full faithfulness on all analytic adic spaces; the seminormal full faithfulness is not planned.

items.name: Rigid analytic points, rigid analytic diamonds and rigid analytic subdiamonds
items.statement: Let L be a non-archimedean field over Q_p and S a diamond over Spd L. (1) A rigid analytic point of S over L is a morphism Spd L' → S over L with L'/L finite. (2) A rigid analytic diamond over Spd L is a diamond isomorphic to Y^♢/Spd L for a seminormal rigid analytic variety Y over L. (3) A rigid analytic subdiamond of S is a locally closed subdiamond that is a rigid analytic diamond over Spd L.

items.name: Classical points of rigid analytic varieties
items.statement: For Y a rigid analytic variety over L, the image in |Y| = |Y^♢| of a rigid analytic point of Y^♢ is a classical point, this gives a bijection between classical points and equivalence classes of rigid analytic points, and the classical points are dense in |Y| (on an affinoid Spa(A, A°) they are the maximal ideals of A).

items.name: Closed rigid analytic subdiamonds are Zariski closed subsets
items.statement: Let Y be a seminormal rigid analytic variety over L. Under |Y| = |Y^♢|, the closed subsets underlying closed rigid analytic subdiamonds of Y^♢ are exactly the Zariski closed subsets of |Y| (the vanishing loci of coherent ideal sheaves).
items.note: The proof uses that perfectoid spaces are uniform (a map factoring through |Z| on points factors through Z^red), properness of a quasi-compact partially proper map of rigid spaces, and BGR §9.6 Proposition 3 (proper images are Zariski closed; AdicSpacesPartII R3 plans Kiehl-type proper finiteness) and BGR 9.5.2 Corollary 7.

items.name: Zariski closed sets of rigid spaces and proper images
items.statement: In a rigid analytic variety Z, the closed sets of the Zariski topology (locally the vanishing sets of finitely many functions on each affinoid) are exactly the vanishing sets of coherent ideal sheaves (BGR 9.5.2, Corollary 7); the image of a proper map of rigid analytic varieties is Zariski closed (BGR §9.6, Proposition 3).
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 3; p. 5, and the proof of Lemma 2.2.3, p. 16
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII R3 constructs coherent ideals and Kiehl-type proper finiteness and coherence.

items.name: Λ-local systems on small v-sheaves
items.statement: For Λ a complete Huber ring, the constant sheaf Λ on Perf is Λ(X) = Cont(|X|, Λ), and the same formula holds for every small v-sheaf X (Mann–Werner, Corollary 3.15). A Λ-local system on X is a sheaf of Λ-modules on X_v that is v-locally isomorphic to Λ^n; Loc_Λ(X) is their full subcategory. For a Q_p-local system on a rigid analytic variety U, a Z_p-lattice exists after an étale cover (Mann–Werner, Proposition 3.10), and profinite torsors are diamonds with finite étale finite levels (ECD Lemma 10.13), so Q_p-local systems on U^♢ descend uniquely to U_ét.
items.locator: Section 2.3, p. 16, and the proof of Theorem 7.2.3, p. 42

items.name: The period sheaves B_dR^+ and B_dR on perfectoid spaces
items.statement: For an affinoid perfectoid Spa(R, R^+) over Q_p, B_dR^+(R) is the Ker θ-adic completion of W(R^{+♭})[1/[ϖ^♭]] for Fontaine's surjection θ, and B_dR(R) inverts a generator of Ker θ; these form v-sheaves B_dR^+ ⊆ B_dR on Perfd_{Q_p} with θ: B_dR^+ → O v-surjective, and over a p-adic field L they are sheaves of algebras over the constant sheaf L.

items.name: B-local systems on affinoid perfectoids are finite projective modules
items.statement: If X = Spa(A, A^+) is affinoid perfectoid over Q_p and B is one of B_dR^+, B_dR, O, then evaluation on X is an equivalence between Loc_B(X) and finite projective B(A)-modules (from the v-stack property, Scholze–Weinstein Corollary 17.1.9).
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry plans descent of finite projective modules on the completed divisor rings.

items.name: The locus where a B_dR-point is integral is Zariski closed
items.statement: Let L be a p-adic field, S = Spa(R, R^+) affinoid perfectoid over Spa L, X an affine scheme of finite type over L and s ∈ X(B_dR(R)). The locus of S over which s lies in X(B_dR^+) is a Zariski closed, hence affinoid perfectoid, subdiamond of S.
items.note: Proof: reduce to X = A^1, where f ∈ Fil^{-i} lies in Fil^{-i+1} exactly on the vanishing set of θ(ξ^i f), and induct; Remark 2.3.3 records the transitivity of Zariski closedness used. Zariski closed subsets of affinoid perfectoids are affinoid perfectoid by Bhatt–Scholze, Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5 (PerfectoidQuotients Q4).

items.name: G(B)-local systems, G(Λ)-local systems and G(Λ)-torsors on diamonds
items.statement: (1) For G a linear algebraic group over a p-adic field L, X a locally spatial diamond over Spd L and B ∈ {O, B_dR^+, B_dR}, a G(B)-local system on X is an exact L-linear tensor functor Rep G → Loc_B(X); the trivial one is ω_std ⊗_L B. (2) For G over Q_p and Λ a complete Huber Q_p-algebra, a G(Λ)-local system is an exact tensor functor Rep G → Loc_Λ(X), and a G(Λ)-torsor is a sheaf on X_v with a right G(Λ)-action v-locally isomorphic to G(Λ).

items.name: G(Λ)-local systems are equivalent to G(Λ)-torsors
items.statement: The groupoids of G(Λ)-local systems and G(Λ)-torsors on X are equivalent, by ρ ↦ Isom(ω_std, ρ) and S ↦ (V ↦ S ×^{G(Λ)} V); a G(Q_p)-torsor is a diamond (ECD Lemma 10.13).

items.name: O-local systems versus vector bundles
items.statement: For X a locally spatial diamond, pullback along X_v → X_ét identifies vector bundles (finite locally free O-modules on X_ét) with the O-local systems trivialized on an étale cover. If X is perfectoid every O-local system is a vector bundle; for X a rigid analytic diamond, vector bundles are those of the seminormal rigid space, O-local systems are locally free Ô-modules on the pro-étale site, and Tate twists give O-local systems that are not vector bundles.

items.name: The de Rham period sheaf OB_dR on the pro-étale site
items.statement: For S a smooth rigid analytic variety over a p-adic field L and ν: S_proét → S_ét, Scholze's period sheaf OB_dR (with the corrigendum) is a filtered ν^{-1}O_{S_ét}-algebra with an integrable connection OB_dR → OB_dR ⊗ Ω^1_S satisfying (OB_dR)^{∇=0} = B_dR compatibly with filtrations, and (OB_dR^+)^{∇=0} = B_dR^+ = Fil^0 OB_dR^{∇=0} (Scholze, Proposition 6.10).

items.name: Scholze's functor from filtered flat bundles to B_dR^+-local systems, and de Rham local systems
items.statement: For S smooth over a p-adic field L, (V, ∇, Fil^•) ↦ M(V, ∇, Fil^•) = Fil^0(ν^{-1}V ⊗_{ν^{-1}O_{S_ét}} OB_dR)^{∇=0} is a fully faithful functor from filtered vector bundles with integrable connection satisfying Griffiths transversality ∇(Fil^i) ⊆ Fil^{i-1} ⊗ Ω^1_S to B_dR^+-local systems on S_proét; Fil^i V ⊗ Ô ≅ (Fil^i L ∩ M)/(Fil^i L ∩ Fil^1 M) (Scholze, Theorem 7.6, Lemma 7.8, Proposition 7.9), and R^1ν_*Ô(1) ≅ Ω^1_S (Scholze, Corollary 6.19). A Q_p-local system 𝕃 on S is de Rham if 𝕃 ⊗ B_dR^+ lies in the essential image of M (equivalently, Scholze's Definition 8.3); then the filtered flat bundle is recovered from 𝕃 and has underlying bundle ν_*(𝕃 ⊗ OB_dR).
items.locator: Section 2.5, p. 18; used in Theorem 3.3.1, p. 23, Theorem 7.2.3, p. 42, and Section 10.1, p. 62

items.name: B_dR^+-local systems on the pro-étale site and on the diamond agree
items.statement: For S smooth over L, the category of B_dR^+-local systems on S_proét is equivalent to that of B_dR^+-local systems on S^♢ (both described, over an étale cover by toric charts with Galois perfectoid covers S̃_i = Spa(A_i, A_i^+), as finite projective B_dR^+(A_i)-modules with the same continuous semilinear descent data for Z_p(1)^n ⋊ Z_p^× and étale descent).

items.name: Hodge and Hodge–Tate analytic structures on basic local Shimura towers (minuscule case)
items.statement: Let [μ] be minuscule, b basic, M_C = M_{b,[μ]} ×_{Spd Q̆_p([μ])} Spd C, 𝔍 = Aut_cont(C/L([μ])). (1) The Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic Zariski topology on M_C is the inverse limit of the rigid analytic Zariski topologies on M_C/K (resp. M_C/K_b) for K ≤ G(Q_p) × 𝔍 (resp. K_b ≤ G_b(Q_p) × 𝔍) compact open. (2) An irreducible Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic set is a connected component of the preimage in M_C of an irreducible locally closed rigid subvariety of some M_C/K (resp. M_C/K_b). (3) A locally closed subdiamond is bi-analytic if it is both. (4) A special subvariety is a connected component of a subdiamond M_{b_H,[μ_H],C} for H ≤ G closed and [μ_H], b_H refining [μ], b up to σ-conjugation.
items.locator: Definition 1.1.2, p. 5; the Zariski topology on a rigid variety is recalled on p. 5
items.note: The general (non-minuscule) forms are Definitions 8.4.1 and 9.1.1, items 154 and 147.

items.name: The two limit presentations of a basic infinite-level moduli space
items.statement: For b basic, M_C = lim_K M_C/K over compact open K ≤ G(Q_p) × 𝔍 and also M_C = lim_{K_b} M_C/K_b over compact open K_b ≤ G_b(Q_p) × 𝔍; the first tower consists of étale covers of Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ],L([μ])} via π_{L_ét} and the second of étale covers of X_{[μ],L([μ])} via π_{L_dR}. For [μ] minuscule the finite levels are smooth rigid analytic varieties over L([μ]); for G reductive they are the basic local Shimura varieties of Scholze–Weinstein.

items.name: Algebraic sources of closed rigid subvarieties of finite-level spaces
items.statement: Let Y = M_C/K over Spd E, E = C^K. (1) If Z ⊆ Fl_{[μ^{-1}],E} is a closed algebraic subvariety, every irreducible component of its preimage under the Hodge period map Y → Fl^{b-adm}_{[μ^{-1}],E} is a closed rigid subvariety of Y. (2) If uniformization gives a map from Y to the basic locus of a global Shimura variety Sh/E, every irreducible component of the preimage of a closed algebraic Z ⊆ Sh is a closed rigid subvariety.

items.name: Special subvarieties from non-reductive subgroups exist even for reductive G
items.statement: For G = GL_4 and μ(z) = diag(z, z, 1, 1), the standard parabolic H with Levi GL_2 × GL_2 gives a special subvariety of the (Lubin–Tate-type) local Shimura varieties of two-dimensional height-four p-divisible formal groups, classifying those that are extensions of one-dimensional height-two formal groups; non-trivial such extensions exist.

items.name: Theorem A(1): the minuscule bi-analytic Ax–Lindemann theorem
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be connected linear algebraic, [μ] minuscule with a basic class [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]), L/Q̆_p a complete discretely valued extension with algebraically closed residue field, C = L̄^ and M_C = M_{b,[μ],C}. The Hodge–Tate (resp. Hodge) analytic Zariski closure of an irreducible Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic set in M_C is a special subvariety.
items.locator: Theorem A, p. 6; proved as the minuscule case of Theorem 9.1.3

items.name: Theorem A(2): special subvarieties are the only closed bi-analytic sets
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem A, special subvarieties are the only closed bi-analytic sets in M_C.

items.name: Ax–Lindemann for algebraic conditions on the Hodge–Tate flag variety
items.statement: Let Z' be an algebraic subvariety of Fl_{[μ],L([μ])} and Z an irreducible component of the rigid variety Z'_C ∩ X_{[μ],C}. Then any connected component Z̃ of π_HT^{-1}(Z) is an irreducible Hodge–Tate analytic set, and the rigid analytic Zariski closure of its image in the finite-level local Shimura variety M_{b,[μ],C}/K is a finite-level special subvariety.

items.name: The zero-dimensional case of Theorem A is Part I's characterization of special points
items.statement: The characterization of the zero-dimensional bi-analytic subvarieties in Theorem A (and in Theorem 9.1.3 in the non-minuscule case) is equivalent to Part I, Corollary C.

items.name: Hyperbolic Ax–Lindemann for Shimura varieties (Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev)
items.statement: Let (G, X^+) be a connected Shimura datum, J: X^+ → Sh_G°(C) = Γ\X^+ the uniformization and X^+ ⊆ Fl_G(C) the period embedding. If Z ⊆ Fl_G is a complex algebraic subvariety and Z_0 an analytic irreducible component of Z(C) ∩ X^+, then the algebraic Zariski closure of J(Z_0) in Sh_G°(C) is a weakly special subvariety. In particular the C-bi-algebraic subvarieties are exactly the weakly special subvarieties.
items.locator: Theorem 1.2.3, p. 8; quoted from Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev 2016, in the formulation of their survey, Theorem 4.28, for comparison

items.name: Neutral admissible pairs over a strict p-adic field are admissible pairs with good reduction
items.statement: If L is a p-adic field with algebraically closed residue field, a neutral admissible pair over Spd L is the same as an admissible pair with good reduction over L (Part I, Section 5.5): Spd L = Spd L̄^/Gal(L̄/L), and the lattices on W ⊗ B_dR coming from filtrations over L are exactly the Galois-stable ones.

items.name: Theorem B(1): generic motivic Galois group and lattice type over a rigid variety
items.statement: Let Z be a geometrically irreducible rigid analytic variety over a strict p-adic field L and A = (W, L_ét) a neutral admissible pair on Z^♢. Then A has a generic motivic Galois group G and is good with lattice invariant [μ], a (not necessarily minuscule) conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p} defined over L.
items.locator: Theorem B, p. 11; proved in Section 9.2, p. 58, from Theorem 7.2.3 and Lemma 9.3.1

items.name: Theorem B(2): density of the Hodge–Tate period image
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem B(1), let C = L̄^, Z̃ → Z_C^♢ a geometric connected component of the associated G(Q_p)-torsor over Z^♢ and π_HT: Z̃ → Fl^♢_{[μ],L([μ])} its Hodge–Tate period map. Then π_HT(Z̃) is rigid Zariski dense in every connected open of Fl^♢_{[μ],L([μ])} that it meets.
items.locator: Theorem B, p. 11; proved in Section 9.2, p. 58

items.name: Filtered O-local systems and their types
items.statement: Let X/Spd Q_p be a locally spatial diamond. A filtered O-local system is an O-local system V with a decreasing filtration F^•V by O-local subsystems such that gr^•V = ⊕_i F^iV/F^{i+1}V is an O-local system and, at each geometric point x, x^*F^iV = 0 for i ≫ 0 and = x^*V for i ≪ 0. The filtration is then locally finite by local direct summands, and its type (the multiset of i counted with rank gr^i) is a locally constant function on |X|. For G = GL_n and μ = (t^{i_1}, …, t^{i_n}) the type is [μ] exactly when rank gr^i V is the multiplicity of i in {i_1, …, i_n} (Example 3.0.2).

items.name: Lattices, latticed B_dR^+-local systems and bilatticed B_dR-local systems
items.statement: For a B_dR-local system V on X, a lattice is a B_dR^+-submodule L ⊆ V that is a B_dR^+-local system with L ⊗ B_dR = V. A latticed B_dR^+-local system is (M, L) with M a B_dR^+-local system and L ⊆ M ⊗ B_dR a lattice; a bilatticed B_dR-local system is (V, L_1, L_2) with two lattices. The two notions are equivalent by M ⊗ B_dR = L ⊗ B_dR ↔ V, M ↔ L_1, L ↔ L_2; Loc^bl_{B_dR}(X) denotes the bilatticed ones.

items.name: The type of a bilatticed B_dR-local system
items.statement: If X = Spa(C, C^+) with C algebraically closed, B_dR^+(C) is a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field C, and the type of a bilatticed B_dR(C)-vector space is the multiset of integers giving the elementary divisors of L_2 relative to L_1 (for GL_n: (M, L) has type (t^{i_1}, …, t^{i_n}) if M has a basis e_j with ξ^{i_j}e_j a basis of L, Example 3.0.1). For general X the type at geometric points is a function on |X|, which need not be locally constant.

items.name: The type of a bilatticed family need not be locally constant
items.statement: On the closed disc D = Spa C_p⟨z⟩ the bilatticed B_dR-module (B_dR^2, (B_dR^+)^2, B_dR^+ e_1 + B_dR^+(e_2 + (z/ξ)e_1)) is well defined (the lattice on the perfectoid cover Spa C_p⟨z^{1/p^∞}⟩ built from [(z, z^{1/p}, …)] is invariant under the covering group because (1 − ε)/ξ ∈ B_dR^+) and has type {1, −1} for z ≠ 0 and type {0, 0} at z = 0.

items.name: The trace filtration and the Bialynicki-Birula functors
items.statement: For a latticed B_dR^+-local system (M, L), trFil^i_L(M ⊗_{B_dR^+} O) := image of (Fil^i B_dR · L) ∩ M in M ⊗ O ≅ ((Fil^i B_dR·L) ∩ M)/((Fil^i B_dR·L) ∩ (Fil^1 B_dR·M)) is a filtration by O-submodules. It gives functors BB_1(V, L_1, L_2) = (L_1 ⊗ O, trFil_{L_2}) and BB_2(V, L_1, L_2) = (L_2 ⊗ O, trFil_{L_1}) from Loc^bl_{B_dR}(X) to O-local systems with a filtration by O-submodules.

items.name: Constant type gives a filtration by local direct summands
items.statement: If a bilatticed B_dR-local system has constant type on X, its trace filtrations are by local direct summands, so BB_1 and BB_2 land in filtered O-local systems; BB_1 inverts the type and BB_2 preserves it (the argument of Scholze–Weinstein, Proposition 19.4.2). Example 3.1.1 shows that without constant type the graded pieces need not be local systems.

items.name: The graded pieces of the two trace filtrations differ by a Tate twist
items.statement: For (V, L_1, L_2) ∈ Loc^bl_{B_dR}(X) and V_i = L_i ⊗_{B_dR^+} O, for each i ∈ Z multiplication induces gr^i_{L_2} V_1 ≅ gr^{-i}_{L_1} V_2(i), where (i) is the tensor product with gr^i B_dR = O ⊗_{Q_p} Q_p(i).

items.name: Filtered, latticed and bilatticed G-local systems and their types
items.statement: Let G/L be connected linear algebraic and X/Spd L a locally spatial diamond. A filtered G(O)-local system is an exact tensor functor from Rep G to filtered O-local systems (sending exact sequences to strict exact sequences); latticed G(B_dR^+)- and bilatticed G(B_dR)-local systems are defined likewise and are equivalent (two G(B_dR^+)-local systems with an isomorphism of their push-outs to G(B_dR)). A filtered G(O)-local system has a locally constant type [μ] with values in Gal(L̄/L)-orbits of conjugacy classes of cocharacters; a bilatticed one has a type function, with an extra value ∅ (no type) when G is not reductive, which may not be locally constant; it is good of type [ν] if this function is constant equal to [ν].

items.name: A bilatticed G-local system is good of type [μ] iff its trace filtrations are filtered G-local systems
items.statement: Let G/L be connected linear algebraic, [μ] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{L̄}, X a diamond over Spd L([μ]) and 𝒢^bl a bilatticed G(B_dR)-local system on X. The following are equivalent: (1) 𝒢^bl is good of type [μ]; (2) BB_1∘𝒢^bl is a filtered G(O)-local system of type [μ^{-1}]; (3) BB_2∘𝒢^bl is a filtered G(O)-local system of type [μ].
items.note: The proof reduces to geometric points (Part I, Theorem 3.2.6, item 006) and argues as in Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 19.4.2 over affinoid perfectoids.

items.name: Semicontinuity of the type, and its failure for non-reductive groups
items.statement: For G reductive, the type of a bilatticed G(B_dR)-local system is lower semicontinuous for the Bruhat order (Scholze–Weinstein, Proposition 19.2.3, after trivializing one lattice). For general G, once the type of the push-out to the Levi quotient is fixed, the locus where a type exists is closed (so ∅ is an open point), but declaring ∅ maximal does not make the type lower semicontinuous: Example 7.5.10 has a type on an open locus and none on its closed complement.

items.name: The trivial-filtration lattice M_0 of a flat bundle
items.statement: For (V, ∇) a vector bundle with integrable connection on a smooth rigid variety X over L, M_0(V, ∇) := M(V, ∇, Fil_triv), Fil_triv^i V = V for i ≤ 0 and 0 for i > 0; it is the extension to the v-site of (ν^{-1}V ⊗ OB_dR^+)^{∇=0}, and the a priori inclusion (ν^{-1}V ⊗ OB_dR^+)^{∇=0} ⊆ (ν^{-1}V ⊗ Fil^0 OB_dR)^{∇=0} is an equality. For every Griffiths-transversal filtration, M(V, ∇, Fil^•) is a B_dR^+-lattice in M_0(V, ∇) ⊗ B_dR.

items.name: Theorem 3.3.1(1): flat bundles embed into B_dR^+-local systems
items.statement: For X/Spa L smooth, (V, ∇) ↦ M_0(V, ∇) is a fully faithful functor from vector bundles with integrable connection on X to B_dR^+-local systems on X^♢, and v_*(M_0(V, ∇) ⊗_{B_dR^+} O) = V under (X^♢_ét, O|_{X^♢_ét}) = (X_ét, O_{X_ét}).

items.name: Theorem 3.3.1(2): Griffiths-transversal filtered flat bundles embed into latticed B_dR^+-local systems
items.statement: (V, ∇, Fil^•) ↦ (M_0(V, ∇), L_Fil), L_Fil := M(V, ∇, Fil^•) ⊆ M_0(V, ∇) ⊗ B_dR, is a fully faithful tensor functor from filtered vector bundles with integrable connection satisfying Griffiths transversality on X to latticed B_dR^+-local systems on X^♢; under (1) the pushforward along v of the trace filtration of L_Fil is Fil^•, and L_Fil is the unique lattice with this property.

items.name: Theorem 3.3.1(3): the essential image is the constant-type locus
items.statement: A latticed B_dR^+-local system (M, L) on X^♢ lies in the essential image of the functor of (2) if and only if M is in the essential image of M_0 and the trace filtration of L on M ⊗ O is by local direct summands (equivalently, the type of L is constant).
items.locator: Theorem 3.3.1, p. 23; part (3), proved by induction on r_1 − r_n using Caraiani–Scholze Proposition 3.4.3, Scholze Corollary 6.19 and Lemma 7.8

items.name: Scholze's functor over a p-adic field
items.statement: For X = Spd L the connection is trivial and (V, Fil^•) ↦ M(V, Fil^•) sends filtered L-vector spaces to Gal(L̄/L)-semilinear B_dR^+(C)-modules (C = L̄^); its essential image is the modules M with dim_L (M ⊗ B_dR(C))^{Gal(L̄/L)} = rank M, and M_0 = (M ⊗ B_dR(C))^{Gal(L̄/L)} ⊗_L B_dR^+(C) is recovered from M.

items.name: Isocrystals, their Dieudonné–Manin classification and the associated bundles
items.statement: Isocrystals (finite-dimensional Q̆_p-spaces with a σ-semilinear bijection) form an exact tensor category classified by Dieudonné–Manin; E ↦ E(W) sends an isocrystal to a vector bundle on each relative curve FF_S, S ∈ Perf_{F̄_p}, by descending the trivial bundle on Y_S along the Frobenius, with slopes of the bundle the negatives of the isocrystal slopes.
items.locator: Section 4.1, p. 26; Section 6.2, p. 37 (the sign of slopes)

items.name: G-isocrystals, B(G) and basic classes for connected linear algebraic G
items.statement: For G/Q_p connected linear algebraic, a G-isocrystal is an exact tensor functor Rep G → Isoc; b ∈ G(Q̆_p) gives V ↦ (V ⊗ Q̆_p, ρ(b)(id ⊗ σ)), inducing a bijection between B(G) (σ-conjugacy classes) and isomorphism classes of G-isocrystals. b is basic if its slope morphism ν_b (Kottwitz) factors through the centre of G; then ν_b is independent of the representative and defined over Q_p, and b is basic if and only if the adjoint isocrystal on Lie G is trivial. B(G)_basic ⊆ B(G) is the set of basic classes.
items.note: BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0 and BG1 plan G-isocrystals, B(G), Newton points and basic classes for reductive G; the non-reductive definitions are new.

items.name: Levi decompositions and B(G): basic in G versus basic in M
items.statement: If G = MU is a Levi decomposition, the inclusion M → G induces B(G) = B(M) with inverse induced by G → M. A basic class of B(G) gives a basic class of B(M), but not conversely: for G the upper-triangular Borel of GL_2 and M the diagonal torus, b = diag(p, 1) is basic in M but not in G (Part I Example 2.2.4).

items.name: The σ-centralizer group G_b
items.statement: For b ∈ G(Q̆_p), G_b(R) = Aut^⊗ of the extension of scalars to Isoc ⊗_{Q_p} R of the G-isocrystal of b; G_b is a linear algebraic group over Q_p with G_b(Q_p) the σ-centralizer of b in G(Q̆_p) (Rapoport–Zink, Proposition 1.12). For b basic, G_b is an inner form of G and G(Q̆_p) = G_b(Q̆_p) canonically.
items.note: BG0 constructs J_b = G_b for reductive G.

items.name: Bun_G for a connected linear algebraic group G
items.statement: For G/Q_p connected linear algebraic, Bun_G is the prestack on Perf_{F̄_p} sending S to the groupoid of G-bundles on FF_S (in any of the equivalent forms of Fargues–Scholze, Definition/Proposition III.1.1); it is a small v-stack (the reductive argument does not use reductivity). For b ∈ G(Q̆_p), E_b: Spd F̄_p → Bun_G is the descent of the trivial G-bundle on Y_S along bσ; Tannakianly, the G-isocrystal of b followed by Isoc → Vect(FF_S).
items.note: BunGAndNewtonStrata BG2:uniformization defines Bun_G for reductive G.

items.name: Automorphisms of E_b and the classifying-stack map
items.statement: For S ∈ Perf_{F̄_p}, the sheaf of sections of G_b × FF_S maps into the automorphism sheaf of E_b on (FF_S)_ét, isomorphically for b basic; since global sections of G_b × FF_S are Cont(|S|, G_b(Q_p)), E_b induces a faithful map [∗/G_b(Q_p)] → Bun_G which is full when b is basic. (Fullness fails in general; the image of b in G/U being basic is necessary but not sufficient.)

items.name: Theorem 4.2.2(1): basic strata of Bun_G are classifying stacks
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be connected linear algebraic. For each [b] ∈ B(G)_basic, the substack Bun_G^{[b]} (G-bundles geometrically isomorphic to E_b) is an open substack of Bun_G, and for any b ∈ [b] the map E_b is an isomorphism [∗/G_b(Q_p)] ≅ Bun_G^{[b]}.
items.note: For G reductive this is Fargues–Scholze Theorem III.4.5, planned in BunGAndNewtonStrata BG3.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.2(2): basic strata are pulled back from the Levi quotient
items.statement: With M = G/U the reductive quotient and [b_M] the image of [b] in B(M), Bun_G^{[b]} ≅ Bun_G ×_{Bun_M} Bun_M^{[b_M]} (push-out of bundles along G → M). The proof shows that every object of the right side is v-locally isomorphic to E_b, by killing the class in H^1_ét(FF_S, 𝒰) (𝒰 an inner form of U) pro-étale locally, inductively along the derived series of U.

items.name: Cohomology of O on the relative curve
items.statement: H^1_ét(FF_S, O) = H^1(FF_S, O) (Kedlaya–Liu, Theorem 8.2.22(c)), and classes in H^1(FF_S, O) are killed pro-étale locally on S (Fargues–Scholze, Proposition II.2.5(ii)).

items.name: Bun_G of an inner twist by a basic class
items.statement: For b ∈ G(Q̆_p) basic, 𝓔 ↦ Isom_{FF_S}(E_b, 𝓔) is an equivalence F_b: Bun_G ≅ Bun_{G_b} (as in Fargues–Scholze III.4.1).

items.name: Twisting exchanges the trivial and basic bundles
items.statement: Writing a_G, a_{G_b} for a ∈ G(Q̆_p) = G_b(Q̆_p), there are natural isomorphisms in Bun_{G_b}(Spd F̄_p): F_b(E_{b_G}) ≅ E_{1_{G_b}} and F_b(E_{1_G}) ≅ E_{b^{-1}_{G_b}}.

items.name: Modifications of G-bundles at the untilt
items.statement: For S ∈ Perf over Spd Q̆_p with untilt ∞: S^♯ → FF_S (a closed Cartier divisor whose completed local ring is B_dR^+), completion gives an exact tensor functor Vect(FF_S) → Loc_{B_dR^+}(S); for E ∈ Bun_G(S) and a lattice L on the G(B_dR)-local system E|_{B_dR}, Beauville–Laszlo gluing gives the modification E_L ∈ Bun_G(S), functorially, interpolating the modifications at geometric points.
items.note: RF4 plans Beauville–Laszlo gluing for vector bundles and its Tannakian transfer to G-torsors (for the reductive groups of BG0); the paper's Tannakian reduction to vector bundles applies to any linear algebraic G.

items.name: The B_dR^+-affine Grassmannian and the flag variety of a connected linear algebraic group
items.statement: Let G/L be connected linear algebraic (L a p-adic field). Gr_G/Spd L is the functor on Perfd_L sending X to isomorphism classes of lattices on the trivial G(B_dR)-local system (equivalently on the trivial G(B_dR^+)-local system); Fl_G/Spa L is the rigid variety whose points on adic spaces X/Spa L are filtrations on the trivial G-bundle on X_ét, and Fl_G^♢ parameterizes filtrations on the trivial G(O)-local system.
items.note: GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0:loop-geometry plans the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannians for reductive G.

items.name: Affine Schubert cells, flag varieties of type [μ] and the Bialynicki-Birula map
items.statement: For [μ] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{L̄} with reflex field L([μ]): Gr_[μ] ⊆ Gr_G ×_{Spd L} Spd L([μ]) parameterizes lattices of type [μ] (at C-points: L(V) = μ(ξ)V_{B_dR^+(C)} for some μ ∈ [μ]_{B_dR^+(C)} and a generator ξ of Fil^1 B_dR^+(C)); Fl_[μ] ⊆ Fl_G ×_{Spa L} Spa L([μ]) parameterizes filtrations of type [μ] (Fil^i V_C = ⊕_{j≥i} V_C[j] for some μ ∈ [μ]_C); and BB: Gr_[μ] → Fl^♢_[μ^{-1}] sends a lattice to its trace filtration (well defined by Theorem 3.2.1). G(B_dR^+) preserves Gr_[μ] and BB is G(B_dR^+)-equivariant.

items.name: Torsor and coset descriptions of Gr_G
items.statement: (1) For X = Spa(A, A^+) affinoid perfectoid, Gr_G(X) is the set of G-torsors on Spec B_dR^+(A) trivialized over Spec B_dR(A). (2) Gr_G is the étale (or v) sheafification of X ↦ G(B_dR(X))/G(B_dR^+(X)); for C algebraically closed, Gr_G(C) = G(B_dR(C))/G(B_dR^+(C)) and, over L([μ]), Gr_[μ](C) = G(B_dR^+(C)) ξ^μ G(B_dR^+(C))/G(B_dR^+(C)).

items.name: Gr_G is a v-sheaf
items.statement: Gr_G is a v-sheaf, and for any diamond X, Gr_G(X) is the set of isomorphism classes of lattices on the trivial G(B_dR)- (equivalently G(B_dR^+)-) local system on X_v (lattices on the trivial local system have no automorphisms).

items.name: Maps from rigid varieties to flag varieties; Fl_[μ] is clopen
items.statement: For S/Spa L seminormal rigid, Hom(S^♢, Fl_G^♢) is the set of filtrations on the trivial G-bundle on S_ét; Fl_[μ] ⊆ Fl_G ×_L Spa L([μ]) is a clopen subvariety.

items.name: Theorem 5.0.4(1): Gr_G is separated, partially proper and ind-(closed locally spatial)
items.statement: Let G/L be connected linear algebraic with unipotent radical U and reductive quotient M. Gr_G is separated and partially proper over Spd L and an increasing union of closed locally spatial subdiamonds.
items.locator: Theorem 5.0.4, p. 31; part (1), proved in Section 5.1
items.note: The proof embeds G as an observable subgroup of a reductive G' (item 020) and applies Lemma 5.1.1 with the reductive case (Scholze–Weinstein Lecture 19; GS0:loop-geometry).

items.name: Theorem 5.0.4(2): Schubert cells are locally closed, and closed when minuscule on the Levi
items.statement: Gr_[μ] ⊆ Gr_G ×_{Spd L} Spd L([μ]) is a locally closed locally spatial subdiamond, partially proper over Spd L([μ]); if [μ]_M is minuscule (weights of Ad∘μ on Lie M in {−1, 0, 1}) it is closed.

items.name: Theorem 5.0.4(3): Gr_[μ] is closed in the preimage of the Levi Schubert cell
items.statement: Gr_[μ] is a closed subdiamond of Gr_G ×_{Gr_M} Gr_{[μ]_M}.
items.locator: Theorem 5.0.4, p. 31; part (3), proved as Proposition 5.2.1

items.name: Theorem 5.0.4(4): maps from rigid varieties see only the Schubert cell, and are Griffiths-transversal filtrations
items.statement: If S/Spa L([μ]) is a seminormal rigid analytic variety, then (Gr_G ×_{Gr_M} Gr_{[μ]_M})(S^♢) = Gr_[μ](S^♢), and BB induces a bijection between this set and the filtrations in Fl_[μ^{-1}](S) satisfying Griffiths transversality over the smooth locus S^sm for the trivial connection on the trivial G-bundle.
items.locator: Theorem 5.0.4, p. 31; part (4), Eq. (5.0.4.1), p. 31; proved in Section 5.3
items.note: Proof: classical points (Part I Proposition 3.1.7(2)), density of classical points and closedness (3); for smooth S, Theorem 3.3.1; in general a resolution of singularities (Temkin) and v-descent.

items.name: Theorem 5.0.4(5): BB is an isomorphism exactly when the weights are at most one
items.statement: If the weights of [μ] on Lie G are ≤ 1, BB: Gr_[μ] → Fl^♢_[μ^{-1}] is an isomorphism. In all other cases the universal filtration on Fl_[μ^{-1}] satisfies Griffiths transversality for the trivial connection over no open subset (a root subgroup of weight > 1 gives a non-transversal direction), so BB has no local section.
items.note: For G reductive and μ minuscule this is Scholze–Weinstein, Theorem 19.4.2; the bijection on points is Part I Proposition 3.1.7(1).

items.name: The affine Grassmannian of the additive group
items.statement: For G = G_a the only cocharacter is trivial and Gr_[μ_triv] = Spd L is the trivial lattice, while Gr_G = B_dR/B_dR^+ = ∪_n t^{-n}B_dR^+/B_dR^+ is enormous; its only rigid analytic point over Spd L is 0, so every map from a rigid analytic diamond to Gr_{G_a} is constant at 0.

items.name: Push-out along a closed subgroup embeds affine Grassmannians
items.statement: Let G' be connected linear algebraic over L and G ≤ G' closed. The push-out Gr_G → Gr_{G'} is injective; if G'/G is quasi-affine it identifies Gr_G with a Zariski locally closed subdiamond of Gr_{G'}, and if G'/G is affine with a Zariski closed one.

items.name: The Bruhat order on conjugacy classes of cocharacters
items.statement: For G with reductive quotient M, choose T ⊆ B ⊆ M_{L̄}; each [μ]_M has a unique B-dominant representative in X_*(T), and [μ_1] ≥ [μ_2] if μ_1 − μ_2 is a non-negative integral combination of B-positive coroots (independent of T and B). Gr_{≤[μ]} (types ≤ [μ] at every geometric point) is closed and proper over Spd L([μ]) for G reductive (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 19.2.3), so Gr_[μ] is open in Gr_{≤[μ]} and closed when [μ] is minuscule.
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry plans bounded Schubert cells, closures, properness and closure relations for reductive G; for general G the order is taken on the reductive quotient.

items.name: Gr_[μ] is cut out by the specialization condition in a faithful representation
items.statement: For every representation ρ: G → GL_n, the restriction of Gr_G → Gr_{GL_n} to Gr_G ×_{Gr_M} Gr_{[μ]_M} lands in the lattices of type ≥ [ρ∘μ]; if ρ is faithful, Gr_[μ] = (Gr_G ×_{Gr_M} Gr_{[μ]_M}) ∩ (Gr_G ×_{Gr_{GL_n}} Gr_{≤[ρ∘μ]}). In particular Gr_[μ] is a closed locally spatial subdiamond of Gr_G ×_{Gr_M} Gr_{[μ]_M}.

items.name: Neutral p-adic Hodge structures over a diamond
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond over Q̆_p. A neutral p-adic Hodge structure on Y is a Q-graded Q_p-vector space V = ⊕_{λ∈Q} V_λ with, for each λ, a B_dR^+-lattice L_λ on V_λ ⊗ B_dR over Y_v such that at every geometric point (V_λ, L_λ) is a p-adic Hodge structure of weight λ (equivalently (V_λ ⊗ O_FF)_{L_λ} is semistable of slope −λ/2 at each geometric point). Example: Q_p(k) = (Q_p, Fil^{-k}B_dR) is the constant Tate structure of weight −2k.

items.name: Neutral p-adic Hodge structures form a neutral Tannakian category
items.statement: The neutral p-adic Hodge structures on Y form a rigid abelian tensor category HS°(Y) over Q_p, neutral Tannakian with fibre functor ω_ét(V, L) = V (as for a point, Part I Theorem 4.3.5).

items.name: Neutral G-p-adic Hodge structures, types and Mumford–Tate groups
items.statement: For G/Q_p connected linear algebraic, a neutral G-p-adic Hodge structure on Y is an exact tensor functor 𝒢: Rep G → HS°(Y) with ω_ét∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std (the isomorphism is not part of the data; with a chosen trivialization it is a p-adic Hodge structure on the trivial G(Q_p)-local system). Its type is the inverse of the type of the associated lattice on the trivial G(B_dR^+)-local system, when that exists. MT(𝒢) = Aut^⊗(ω_ét|_⟨𝒢⟩) is a linear algebraic group over Q_p, a closed subgroup of G after trivialization, and 𝒢 has a canonical MT(𝒢)-structure.
items.locator: Definition 6.1.1, p. 36; Remark 6.1.2 and Section 6.1, p. 36

items.name: The period domain X_[μ]
items.statement: Fix a Levi decomposition G = M ⋉ U and let L_univ be the universal lattice on the trivial G(B_dR^+)-local system over Gr_[μ^{-1}]; the modification (E_triv)_{L_univ} is a Gr_[μ^{-1}]-point of Bun_G. If the unique basic element [b] of B(M, [μ^{-1}]) is basic in G, X_[μ] := Gr_[μ^{-1}] ×_{Bun_G} Bun_G^{[b]}.

items.name: X_[μ] is a non-empty open subdiamond of Gr_[μ^{-1}]
items.statement: X_[μ] ⊆ Gr_[μ^{-1}] is a non-empty open subdiamond; moreover X_[μ]/Spd Q̆_p([μ]) admits a rigid analytic point.
items.note: Openness by Theorem 4.2.2; non-emptiness by Part I Example 5.4.6 and Theorem 5.1.6; the rigid point by Proposition 7.3.3 and Theorem 8.5.1.

items.name: X_[μ] is the moduli space of p-adic Hodge structures of type [μ] on the trivial G(Q_p)-local system
items.statement: Let ν be the slope morphism of [b]. The restriction of L_univ on ω_std to X_[μ], with weight grading induced by 2ν, is the universal p-adic Hodge structure of type [μ] and weight 2ν on the trivial G(Q_p)-local system.

items.name: X_[μ] is geometrically connected
items.statement: X_[μ] is geometrically connected.
items.locator: Proposition 6.2.3, p. 37; second assertion; from Theorem 8.5.1 and Proposition 7.3.4

items.name: The Hodge–Tate locus of a line
items.statement: Let 𝒢 be a p-adic Hodge structure on the trivial G(Q_p)-local system over a locally spatial diamond S/Q̆_p, V ∈ Rep G with 𝒢(V) = (V, L), and ℓ ⊆ V_{2n} a line in weight 2n. HT(ℓ) ⊆ S is the subfunctor of f: Y → S with ℓ ⊗_{Q_p} Fil^n B_dR ⊆ f^*L; it is the locus where ℓ underlies a sub-structure (isomorphic to Q_p(−n) = (Q_p, Fil^n B_dR)).

items.name: Hodge–Tate loci are closed
items.statement: HT(ℓ) ⊆ S is a closed subdiamond.
items.locator: Lemma 6.3.2, p. 38; first assertion; by Lemma 2.3.2

items.name: The Hodge–Tate locus is where the Mumford–Tate group stabilizes the line
items.statement: HT(ℓ) is the locus where MT(𝒢|_{HT(ℓ)}) ⊆ Stab_G(ℓ): a map f: T → S with MT(f^*𝒢) ⊆ Stab_G(ℓ) factors through HT(ℓ).

items.name: Hodge–Tate loci on rigid analytic varieties are Zariski closed
items.statement: Let L/Q̆_p([μ]) be a p-adic field, S/Spa L seminormal rigid analytic and 𝒢 a p-adic Hodge structure of type [μ] on the trivial G(Q_p)-local system over S^♢. For ℓ as above, HT(ℓ) ⊆ S^♢ is rigid analytic, i.e. a Zariski closed subset of S: it is the vanishing locus of a basis vector of ℓ in V ⊗ O_{S_ét}/Fil^{-n} for the Hodge–Tate filtration of Theorem 3.3.1.

items.name: Functoriality of period domains for subgroups
items.statement: Let H ≤ G be closed and [μ_H] ⊆ [μ] a class of cocharacters of H with a basic class [b_H] ∈ B(H, [μ_H^{-1}]) whose image in B(G) is basic. Then that image is the basic class of B(G, [μ^{-1}]), and there is an injective functoriality map X_[μ_H] ↪ X_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ_H])}.

items.name: Period domains of subgroups are closed when minuscule on the Levi
items.statement: If H = M_H ⋉ U_H is a Levi decomposition and [μ_H] is M_H-minuscule, X_[μ_H] is a closed subdiamond of X_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ_H])}; in particular this holds if [μ_H] has weights ≥ −1 on Lie H, and then X_[μ_H] is rigid analytic (an open in Fl^♢_[μ_H]).
items.locator: Proposition 6.4.1, p. 39; and the paragraph after it, p. 39

items.name: Special subvarieties of X_[μ]
items.statement: For C/Q̆_p algebraically closed non-archimedean, a special subvariety of X_{[μ],C} is a closed rigid analytic subdiamond of the form X_{[μ_H],C} with [μ_H] of weights ≥ −1 on Lie H.

items.name: Neutral admissible pairs over a diamond
items.statement: For Y/Spd Q̆_p a locally spatial diamond, a neutral admissible pair is (W, L_ét) with W an isocrystal and L_ét a B_dR^+-lattice in W ⊗ B_dR over Y such that every geometric restriction is an admissible pair (equivalently E(W)_{L_ét} on the relative curve is semistable of slope 0); morphisms are isocrystal maps f with f_{B_dR}(L) ⊆ L'. AdmPair°(Y) has tensor products and duals.

items.name: Neutral admissible pairs form a neutral Tannakian category
items.statement: AdmPair°(Y) is a neutral Tannakian category over Q_p with fibre functor ω_y(W, L) = H^0(FF_{C♭}, E(W)_{y^*L}) for any geometric point y: Spd(C, C^+) → Y (images and coimages agree by a slope argument at geometric points; ω_y is faithful because a morphism is determined by its map of isocrystals).

items.name: Realizations of neutral admissible pairs
items.statement: On AdmPair°(Y): the isocrystalline realization ω_Isoc(W, L) = W; the étale realization ω_ét(W, L) = H^0(FF_Y, E(W)_L) in Loc_{Q_p}(Y), an exact tensor functor by the equivalence of slope-zero bundles with Q_p-local systems; the de Rham comparison c_dR: ω_ét ⊗ B_dR ≅ ω_Isoc ⊗ B_dR; the étale lattice ω_{L_ét}(W, L) = L on ω_Isoc ⊗ B_dR; and the de Rham lattice L_dR(W, L) = c_dR^{-1}(W ⊗ B_dR^+) on ω_ét ⊗ B_dR. Example: the Tate pair Q̆_p(n) = ((Q̆_p, p^{-n}φ), Fil^n B_dR).

items.name: Slope-zero bundles on relative curves are Q_p-local systems
items.statement: Vector bundles on the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve that are semistable of slope zero at every geometric point are equivalent to Q_p-local systems (Kedlaya–Liu; Fargues–Scholze, Corollary II.2.20), compatibly with tensor products.

items.name: Neutral G-admissible pairs and their motivic Galois groups
items.statement: A neutral G-admissible pair on Y is an exact tensor functor 𝒢: Rep G → AdmPair°(Y) with ω_y∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std for each geometric point y. For y a geometric point, MG(𝒢, y) = Aut^⊗(ω_y|_⟨𝒢⟩) is a linear algebraic group over Q_p, a closed subgroup of G after a trivialization ω_y∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std, and 𝒢 has a canonical refinement to MG(𝒢, y)-structure. A choice of ω_Isoc∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std ⊗ Q̆_p makes ω_{L_ét}∘𝒢 a lattice on the trivial G(B_dR)-local system, with classifying map Y → Gr_{G,Q̆_p}.

items.name: The type of a neutral G-admissible pair
items.statement: For Y/Spd Q̆_p([μ]), 𝒢 has type [μ] if the classifying map Y → Gr_{G,Q̆_p([μ])} factors through Gr_[μ] (independent of the trivialization, since Gr_[μ] is G(Q̆_p)-stable). Then the Hodge filtration on (ω_Isoc∘𝒢) ⊗ O has type [μ^{-1}] and the Hodge–Tate filtration on ω_ét ⊗ O (from the de Rham lattice) has type [μ].

items.name: Liu–Zhu rigidity: being de Rham can be checked at one classical point
items.statement: For a Q_p-local system on a connected smooth rigid analytic variety over a p-adic field, if its stalk at one classical point is de Rham then it is de Rham (Liu–Zhu, Theorem 3.9(iv)).
items.note: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6:comparison owns 'the regularity, boundary extension, and arithmetic rigidity statements used by Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu', which is this theorem (the Liu–Zhu extraction also routes it there).

items.name: Neutral G-admissible pairs on geometrically connected rigid varieties have a type
items.statement: If L/Q̆_p is a p-adic field and S/Spa L a geometrically connected seminormal rigid analytic variety, every neutral G-admissible pair on S^♢ has a type.
items.note: Proof: each ω_ét∘𝒢(V) descends to S_ét and is de Rham (Liu–Zhu rigidity and Part I Theorem 5.5.1 at a classical point); its filtered flat bundle is V ⊗ O_{S_ét} with a filtration whose lattice is ω_{L_ét}∘𝒢. The argument as written uses tools for smooth S; see source issue E13.

items.name: b-rigidifications and the b-admissible locus
items.statement: For b ∈ G(Q̆_p), a b-rigidification of a neutral G-admissible pair 𝒢 is an isomorphism ρ_Isoc: W_b ≅ ω_Isoc∘𝒢, W_b the G-isocrystal V ↦ (V_{Q̆_p}, bφ). Gr_G^{b-adm} ⊆ Gr_{G,Q̆_p} is the preimage of the open substack Bun_G^{[1]} under L ↦ (E_b)_L (the locus where the modification is the trivial G-bundle), and Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} := Gr_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ])} ×_{Gr_G} Gr_G^{b-adm}.

items.name: Gr_G^{b-adm} represents b-rigidified admissible pairs
items.statement: Pullback of the universal pair (b, L_univ) induces Gr_G^{b-adm}(S) = {(𝒢, ρ_Isoc): 𝒢 ∈ G-AdmPair°(S), ρ_Isoc: W_b ≅ ω_Isoc∘𝒢}/≅, and Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} parameterizes b-rigidified admissible pairs of type [μ].

items.name: The b-admissible locus is open
items.statement: Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} is open in Gr_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ])}.

items.name: Reductive case: non-emptiness of admissible loci
items.statement: For G reductive, Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} ≠ ∅ implies [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]) (Caraiani–Scholze, Proposition 3.5.3), and if [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]) the admissible locus has a rigid analytic point (Rapoport–Viehmann, Proposition 3.1).

items.name: The b-admissible locus is non-empty exactly for [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]), and then has a rigid point
items.statement: Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} is non-empty if and only if [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]); when non-empty, Gr_[μ]^{b-adm}/Spd Q̆_p([μ]) admits a rigid analytic point (the printed statement names Gr_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ])}; see source issue E7).
items.note: Reduced to the Levi quotient via M → G → M (identity on admissible loci).

items.name: Reductive case: connectedness of admissible loci (Gleason–Lourenço)
items.statement: For G reductive, the open cells Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} (and the closed cells Gr_{≤[μ]}^{b-adm}) are geometrically connected (Gleason–Lourenço, proof of Theorem 3.2).

items.name: Cohomological smoothness of Schubert cells and truncated positive loop groups
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed C, the open Schubert cells Gr_{[μ_M],C} of a reductive M and the groups U(B_dR^+/Fil^m B_dR^+) (U unipotent) are ℓ-cohomologically smooth and connected over Spd C (Fargues–Scholze VI.2.4 and IV.1.18).
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness plans truncated positive loop groups and the ℓ-cohomological smoothness of open cells.

items.name: The b-admissible locus is geometrically connected
items.statement: Gr_[μ]^{b-adm}/Spd Q̆_p([μ]) is geometrically connected. (For G = MU, U(B_dR^+) preserves Gr_[μ]^{b-adm}, its action factors through U(B_dR^+/Fil^m) once m exceeds the weights of μ on Lie U, and U(B_dR^+/Fil^m) × Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ_M],C} → Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ],C} is surjective on points.)

items.name: Six-functor identities and the Künneth formula for diamonds
items.statement: For f: X → Y cohomologically smooth, Rf^!F_ℓ is invertible, Rf^!(K) = Rf^!F_ℓ ⊗ f^*K and exceptional pullback composes (ECD Proposition 23.12(i),(iii)); Rf_! satisfies the Künneth formula for fibre products over Spd C (Hansen, Proposition 4.2).
items.note: The Künneth formula for Rf_! follows from base change (ECD 22.19) and the projection formula (22.23), planned in S2; 23.12 is planned in S4.

items.name: Products of connected cohomologically smooth diamonds are connected
items.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed non-archimedean extension of Q_p and X, Y locally spatial diamonds that are ℓ-cohomologically smooth over Spd C and connected. Then X ×_{Spd C} Y is connected. (A cohomologically smooth S/Spd C is connected iff R^0f_!Rf^!F_ℓ = F_ℓ.)

items.name: The Hodge locus of a rank-one sub-isocrystal
items.statement: Let 𝒢 = (W_b, L) be a b-rigidified G-admissible pair on S/Q̆_p, V ∈ Rep G and ℓ ⊆ V_{Q̆_p} underlying a sub-isocrystal ℓ ≅ Q̆_p(n) = (Q̆_p, p^{-n}φ) of W_b(V). Hdg(ℓ)(Y) = {f: Y → S : ℓ ⊗ Fil^n B_dR ⊆ f^*L(V)} (inside V ⊗ B_dR(Y)), the locus where ℓ underlies a sub-admissible pair; equivalently where (ℓ, (ℓ ⊗ B_dR) ∩ f^*L(V)) is in AdmPair°(Y).

items.name: Hodge loci do not depend on the representative of [b]
items.statement: If b' = gbσ(g)^{-1} with g ∈ G(Q̆_p), the isomorphism Gr_G^{b-adm} ≅ Gr_G^{b'-adm}, L ↦ gL, restricts to Hdg(ℓ) ≅ Hdg(g·ℓ).

items.name: Hodge loci are closed
items.statement: Hdg(ℓ) ⊆ S is a closed subdiamond.

items.name: Hodge loci on rigid analytic varieties are Zariski closed
items.statement: Let L/Q̆_p([μ]) be a p-adic field, S/Spa L seminormal rigid analytic and 𝒢 a b-rigidified admissible pair of type [μ] on S^♢. Then Hdg(ℓ) ⊆ S^♢ is rigid analytic, i.e. corresponds to a Zariski closed subset of S.

items.name: Functoriality maps between admissible loci
items.statement: For f: H → G a homomorphism of connected linear algebraic groups, b_H ∈ H(Q̆_p), b_G ∈ G(Q̆_p) and g ∈ G(Q̆_p) with g f(b_H) σ(g^{-1}) = b_G, push-out composed with the Hecke action of g gives Gr_H^{b_H-adm} → Gr_G^{b_G-adm}, L ↦ g·(L ×^H G), whose value at V ∈ Rep G is the lattice g L(f^*V).

items.name: Reduction to the motivic Galois group factors the classifying map
items.statement: Let 𝒢 on Y be induced by f: Y → Gr_G^{b-adm}, y a geometric point and H = MG(𝒢, y) ≤ G with canonical reduction ℋ. (1) There is b_H ∈ H(Q̆_p) with [b_H] ⊆ [b] such that f factors through a functoriality map f': Y → Gr_H^{b_H-adm}, and f'^* of the universal neutral H-admissible pair is ℋ.

items.name: Over a geometrically connected rigid base the reduction lands in one Schubert cell
items.statement: If moreover Y is a geometrically connected rigid analytic diamond over a p-adic field, any f' as in Lemma 7.5.1(1) factors through an open Schubert cell Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H]} with μ_H a cocharacter of H contained in [μ].

items.name: Admissible loci of closed subgroups are closed subdiamonds
items.statement: For H ≤ G closed and b_H, b_G, g as in the functoriality construction, the functoriality map identifies Gr_H^{b_H-adm} with a closed subdiamond of Gr_G^{b_G-adm}, namely the Hodge locus Hdg(ℓ_{Q̆_p}) of a line ℓ with H = Stab(ℓ). (Although Gr_H → Gr_G need not be closed for non-reductive H: for the Borel of GL_2, b = diag(p, 1) and μ = diag(t^{-1}, 1), it is A^1 → P^1 on Schubert cells but A^1 ≅ A^1 on admissible loci.)

items.name: Special subdiamonds of admissible loci
items.statement: A special subdiamond of Gr_G^{b_G-adm} is a closed subdiamond identified with some Gr_H^{b_H-adm} by a functoriality map.

items.name: Schubert cells with weights at most one in admissible loci are closed rigid analytic
items.statement: If the weights of [μ_H] on Lie H are ≤ 1, then Gr_[μ_H]^{b_H-adm} is a geometrically connected rigid analytic diamond over Q̆_p([μ_H]), closed in Gr^{b_H-adm}_{H,Q̆_p([μ_H])}; via functoriality it is a closed geometrically connected rigid analytic subdiamond of Gr^{b_G-adm}_{G,Q̆_p([μ_H])}, inside Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ_G],Q̆_p([μ_H])}.
items.locator: Lemma 7.5.5, p. 48; and the paragraph after it, p. 48

items.name: Special subvarieties of admissible loci
items.statement: For C/Q̆_p algebraically closed, a special subvariety of Gr^{b_G-adm}_{G,C} or Gr^{b_G-adm}_{[μ_G],C} is a closed connected rigid analytic subdiamond identified with some Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H],C} for [μ_H] with weights ≤ 1 on Lie H; those from tori are special points.

items.name: The Kottwitz map for tori
items.statement: For a torus T, Kottwitz's map κ_T: B(T) → X_*(T)_{Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p)} is an isomorphism, and B(T, [μ]) is the single class b_μ with κ_T([b_μ]) = μ^#.

items.name: Admissible loci of tori
items.statement: For a torus T, Gr_[μ] = Gr_[μ]^{b_{μ^{-1}}-adm} is a single point, and for b ∈ T(Q̆_p), Gr_T^{b-adm} = ⊔_{μ: μ^# = κ_T([b])} Gr_[μ^{-1}].

items.name: Special subvarieties move in G_b(Q_p)-families; the Lubin–Tate example
items.statement: The special subvarieties attached to (H, [μ_H]) depend only on its G(Q_p)-conjugacy class but vary with the element g σ-conjugating b_H to b_G, i.e. under G_b(Q_p). In the height-two Lubin–Tate case (admissible locus P^1_{Q̆_p}) with H = F^×, F/Q_p quadratic, the special points (formal groups with endomorphisms by F) form one G_b(Q_p)-orbit identified with P^1(F), G_b(Q_p) the units of the quaternion division algebra.

items.name: Intersections of admissible loci with Schubert cells
items.statement: If H is reductive, the classes [μ_H] refining [μ] are incomparable in the Bruhat order and (after a finite extension) Gr^{b_H-adm}_{H,Q̆_p([μ])} ∩ Gr_[μ]^{b_G-adm} = ⊔_{[μ_H]⊆[μ]} Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H]}; the special subvarieties of Gr_[μ]^{b_G-adm} are the rigid analytic connected components of such intersections. For non-reductive H, Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H]} need not be closed in Gr_H^{b_H-adm} ∩ Gr_[μ_G]^{b_G-adm}.

items.name: A non-closed special cell inside a Schubert cell
items.statement: Let G = GL_3, H the parabolic stabilizing ⟨e_1, e_2⟩ with Levi GL_2 × GL_1, and on D_C = Spa C⟨z⟩ let L_z = ⟨e_1, e_2 + (z/ξ)e_1, e_3 + (1/ξ)e_1⟩ = ⟨ξe_3, e_2 − ze_3, (1/ξ)(ξe_3 + e_1)⟩. Then (Q̆_p^3, L_z) is a neutral admissible pair (b = 1), L_z ∈ Gr_[μ] for μ = (t, 1, t^{-1}), L_z ∈ Gr_H^{1-adm}, for z ≠ 0 L_z ∈ Gr^{1-adm}_{[μ_H],H} with μ_H = (t, t^{-1}) × 1, but L_0 ∉ Gr_{[μ_H],H}; so Gr^{1-adm}_{[μ_H]} is not closed in Gr_H^{1-adm} ∩ Gr_[μ]^{1-adm}.

items.name: The infinite-level moduli space M_b
items.statement: For G/Q_p connected linear algebraic and b ∈ G(Q̆_p), M_b/Spd Q̆_p classifies (𝒢, ρ_Isoc, ρ_ét) with 𝒢 a neutral G-admissible pair, ρ_Isoc: W_b ≅ ω_Isoc∘𝒢 and ρ_ét: ω_std ⊗ Q_p ≅ ω_ét∘𝒢. The forgetful map π_{L_ét}: M_b → Gr_G^{b-adm} is the G(Q_p)-torsor Isom(ω_std ⊗ Q_p, ω_ét∘𝒢), so M_b is a locally spatial diamond; M_{b,[μ]} := M_b ×_{Gr_G^{b-adm}} Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} is a locally closed subdiamond of M_{b,Q̆_p([μ])}.

items.name: M_b is the moduli of modifications from E_b to the trivial bundle
items.statement: A modification α: E_b ⇢ E_triv (an isomorphism off ∞ with locally bounded poles) gives the lattice π_{L_ét}(α) = α_{B_dR}^{-1}(E_triv|_{B_dR^+}) ⊆ W_b ⊗ B_dR and a b-rigidified admissible pair with canonical étale and isocrystalline trivializations; this identifies M_b(S) with the set of modifications E_b ⇢ E_triv over S.

items.name: The period maps of M_{b,[μ]}
items.statement: π_{L_ét}(𝒢, ρ_ét, ρ_Isoc) = ρ_Isoc^*((ω_ét∘𝒢) ⊗ B_dR^+) and π_{L_dR}(𝒢, ρ_ét, ρ_Isoc) = ρ_ét^*((ω_Isoc∘𝒢) ⊗ B_dR^+), lattices on ω_std ⊗ B_dR, give M_b → Gr_G (twice); on M_{b,[μ]} they land in Gr_[μ] and Gr_[μ^{-1}], and composing with BB gives the Hodge and Hodge–Tate period maps π_Hdg: M_{b,[μ]} → Fl_[μ^{-1}] and π_HT: M_{b,[μ]} → Fl_[μ]. For b basic, ρ_ét^*L_dR is a p-adic Hodge structure on the trivial G(Q_p)-local system and π_{L_dR} factors through X_[μ].

items.name: For b basic, π_{L_dR} is a G_b(Q_p)-torsor over X_[μ]
items.statement: For b basic, π_{L_dR}: M_{b,[μ]} → X_[μ] is a G_b(Q_p)-torsor; in particular the G_b(Q_p)-action by change of ρ_Isoc extends to an action of the topological constant sheaf G_b(Q_p) (clear from the modification description).

items.name: Functoriality maps of infinite-level moduli spaces
items.statement: For ι: H ↪ G closed connected, [μ_H] ⊆ [μ], b_H ∈ H(Q̆_p) representing the basic class of B(H, [μ_H^{-1}]) and g ∈ G(Q̆_p) with g^{-1}bσ(g) = b_H, push-out and g: E_{ι(b_H)} ≅ E_b give M_{b_H,[μ_H]} → M_{b,[μ],Q̆_p([μ_H])}, Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H]} → Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ_H])} and, for b basic, X_[μ_H] → X_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ_H])}, compatibly with group actions and period maps.

items.name: Hodge and Hodge–Tate special subvarieties at infinite level
items.statement: Let [μ] admit a basic class [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]), L/Q̆_p([μ]) a p-adic field, C = L̄^, M = M_{b,[μ]}. (1) A Hodge special subvariety of M_C is a connected component of a closed subdiamond M_{b_H,[μ_H],C} with [μ_H] of weights ≤ 1 on Lie H; equivalently a connected component of the π_{L_ét}-preimage of a special subvariety Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H],C}. (2) For b basic, a Hodge–Tate special subvariety is a connected component of such an M_{b_H,[μ_H],C} with weights ≥ −1 on Lie H; equivalently of the π_{L_dR}-preimage of a special subvariety X_{[μ_H],C} of X_{[μ],C}.

items.name: Special subvarieties at infinite level
items.statement: A special subvariety of M_C is a connected component of a closed subdiamond M_{b_H,[μ_H],C} with [μ_H] minuscule on Lie H (weights in [−1, 1]).

items.name: Special means both Hodge special and Hodge–Tate special
items.statement: If b is basic, a closed connected subdiamond of M_C is a special subvariety if and only if it is both a Hodge special and a Hodge–Tate special subvariety (take H the motivic Galois group, equivalently the Mumford–Tate group, of the universal pair restricted to it).

items.name: When the three notions of special subvariety agree
items.statement: If [μ] is minuscule, Hodge special subvarieties and special subvarieties coincide, and for b basic they are also the Hodge–Tate special subvarieties, with no weight condition needed; the three notions also agree when H is reductive.

items.name: A Hodge special subvariety that is not Hodge–Tate special
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be a cubic extension, G = Res_{E/Q_p} GL_2 and H ≤ G the mirabolic subgroup (* *; 0 1) = E^× ⋉ E. With E^×_{Q̄_p} = G_m^3 and μ_H = μ: t ↦ (t, t, t^{-2}), the basic elements are b_H = b = 1, and the associated Hodge special subvariety is not Hodge–Tate special (the weights of μ_H on Lie H are 0, 1, 1, −2).

items.name: Basic duality: M_b ≅ M_{b^{-1}} for the inner form G_b
items.statement: Let b ∈ G(Q̆_p) be basic. Then b_{G_b}^{-1} is basic in G_b(Q̆_p), and twisting by F_b (a modification E_triv ⇢ E_b becomes E_{b^{-1}_{G_b}} ⇢ E_triv via Lemma 4.2.3) is a G(Q_p) × G_b(Q_p)-equivariant isomorphism M_b ≅ M_{b^{-1}_{G_b}} exchanging the de Rham and étale lattice period maps.
items.note: For GL_n and the Lubin–Tate/Drinfeld towers this is the Faltings–Fargues isomorphism planned in EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6a; the PEL normalization differs by a transpose (Remark 8.5.2).

items.name: Basic duality exchanges the Hodge and Hodge–Tate structures
items.statement: For each [μ] such that [b] is the basic element of B(G, [μ^{-1}]), the duality restricts to M_{b,[μ]} ≅ M_{b^{-1}_{G_b},[μ^{-1}]}, exchanging the Hodge and Hodge–Tate period maps and the Hodge and Hodge–Tate special subvarieties.

items.name: Hodge and Hodge–Tate analytic Zariski closures, irreducible analytic sets and bi-analytic sets
items.statement: Let M = M_{b,[μ]} with [b] basic in B(G, [μ^{-1}]), L/Q̆_p([μ]) a p-adic field, C = L̄^, 𝔍 = Gal(L̄/L). For A ⊂ |M_C| the Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic Zariski closure is the intersection of all preimages of closed rigid analytic subdiamonds (over C^K) of M_C/K containing A, K ≤ G(Q_p) × 𝔍 (resp. K ≤ G_b(Q_p) × 𝔍) compact open. An irreducible Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic set is a connected component of the preimage of an irreducible locally closed rigid analytic subdiamond of some M_C/K; a locally closed subdiamond is bi-analytic if it is both. (In the minuscule case these closures are the closures for the limit Zariski topologies; in general it is unclear whether finite unions of closed rigid analytic subdiamonds are rigid analytic.)

items.name: Theorem 9.1.3(1): special subvarieties are Zariski closed irreducible analytic sets
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be connected linear algebraic, [μ] admitting a basic class [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]), b ∈ [b] and M = M_{b,[μ]}. Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) special subvarieties are Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) Zariski closed irreducible Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic sets in M_C.

items.name: Theorem 9.1.3(2): the bi-analytic Ax–Lindemann theorem
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 9.1.3, the Hodge–Tate (resp. Hodge) analytic Zariski closure of an irreducible Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic set is a Hodge–Tate (resp. Hodge) special subvariety, unless the defining intersection is indexed by the empty set (in which case it is all of M_C).

items.name: Theorem 9.1.3: the closed bi-analytic sets are the special subvarieties
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 9.1.3, special subvarieties are the only closed bi-analytic sets in M_C.

items.name: Without the basic hypothesis special subvarieties need not be Hodge–Tate closed
items.statement: For the generic fibre of the Serre–Tate deformation space of μ_{p^∞} × Q_p/Z_p (G the upper-triangular group, μ = diag(z^{-1}, 1), b = diag(p, 1)), the Hodge–Tate period map has one-point image, so the special point of the canonical lift (the diagonal torus) cannot be cut out by conditions on the Hodge–Tate filtration.

items.name: The Hodge–Tate period map is a submersion at a Hodge-generic classical point
items.statement: In the proof of Theorem 9.1.3(2), after reducing to G = H the motivic Galois group: let Y be a connected closed rigid analytic subdiamond of M_C/K_b containing the image of Z̃, z ∈ Z(C) a Hodge-generic classical point with image y. Then an open subgroup of 𝔍 moves y through an orbit K_0·y of a compact open K_0 ≤ G(Q_p) (Part I Corollary 5.5.3 and Lemma 9.3.3); for a smooth locally closed V ⊆ Y containing K_0·y on which df has constant rank k, with f: V → Fl_{[μ],E} induced by BB∘π_{L_dR}, one has k = dim Fl_[μ] (a function vanishing on the orbit K_0·f(y) of the submersive orbit map vanishes near f(y)). Hence df_y is surjective, Griffiths transversality forces the weights of [μ] on Lie G to be ≥ −1, M_C/K_b is étale over Fl^♢_{[μ],E}, and dimension count gives that Y is the connected component of M_C/K_b through y.
items.locator: Section 9.2, p. 56; proof of Theorem 9.1.3, pp. 57–58

items.name: Lemma 9.3.1: Hodge-generic classical points are dense
items.statement: Let L/Q̆_p be a p-adic field, Z/Spa L a geometrically irreducible rigid analytic variety and 𝒢 a neutral G-admissible pair over Z^♢. Then the Hodge generic locus of 𝒢 in |Z| = |Z^♢| contains a dense set of classical points.
items.locator: Lemma 9.3.1, p. 58; deduced from Lemma 9.3.5 on a desingularization of Z

items.name: The Hodge exceptional and Hodge generic loci
items.statement: For a neutral admissible pair 𝒢 on a locally spatial diamond S over Spd Q̆_p, the Hodge exceptional locus is the union of all strictly contained Hodge loci |Hdg(ℓ)| ⊊ |S|, ℓ running over rank-one sub-isocrystals of ω_Isoc(V) for all V ∈ Rep G; the Hodge generic locus is its complement (which may be empty in general).

items.name: Meeting the Hodge generic locus means having the full motivic Galois group
items.statement: A subdiamond T ⊆ S meets the Hodge generic locus of 𝒢 if and only if MG(𝒢|_T, y) = MG(𝒢, y) for some (equivalently any) geometric point y of T.

items.name: The Hodge exceptional locus is a countable union of closed subsets
items.statement: Let S be a locally spatial diamond over Spd Q̆_p and 𝒢 a b-rigidified neutral G-admissible pair on S. The Hodge exceptional locus of 𝒢 is a countable union of closed subsets of |S|. (For V ∈ Rep G and V_k = W_b(V)^{φ=p^{-k}}, the incidence subdiamond I_{V_k} ⊆ P_{V_k}(Q_p) × S of pairs (ℓ, s) with s ∈ Hdg(ℓ) is closed; the lines with Hdg(ℓ) ≠ S form an open set, a countable union of compact opens K_i, and the images of |I_{K_i}| under the proper projection are closed.)

items.name: Baire category theorem
